interpretation: Instruction (from ep.observe): 'Pick up the green tape and place it on the black shelf'. Green tape = obj1, a green tape roll lying flat on the table at about (0.253, -0.007): an annulus with outer radius about 4.5 cm, inner radius about 3.3 cm, 2.5 cm tall. Black shelf = obj2, a solid black box 26x14x8 cm whose flat top (z = 0.080) spans x 0.360-0.499, y -0.148-0.112 (measured from its top-face points; the perceived centroid 0.417 was biased toward the visible side face). Goal: the tape resting on the shelf's top surface, released by the gripper. The box has no shelf levels, so its top face is the only place to put the tape. The tape (9 cm across) is wider than the gripper's max_width_m (6.6 cm), so it had to be gripped by its 1.2 cm wall, one finger in the hole and one outside.
plan: Initial plan: grip the rim top-down on the ring's -y side, with the closing axis radial (world y) and the TCP over the wall centre line (r = 3.87 cm) at z = 0.027 (fingertips 7 mm above the table). Then lift, carry over the shelf, lower the tape to about 5 mm above the shelf top at its centre, open, and retreat straight up. The +x side was rejected because link6 hit the shelf there. Change 1: the straight lift to z = 0.17 was refused as unreachable, and an IK sweep showed top-down poses reach only z <= 0.13 near the ring and z <= 0.08 over the shelf centre. So I placed with the gripper pitched 15-25 deg about its closing axis, which keeps a radially gripped ring's centre fixed. Change 2: the closing had rotated the ring in the grip (its centre ended up at TCP + (0.022, 0.032) instead of (0, 0.039)). I re-measured the held ring from colour-filtered scene-camera points, rebuilt its geometry model, and compensated the arm's tracking error. Change 3: on the first release the ring hung on the open gripper. I tried to free it, re-gripped it, re-placed it flat (5 deg pitch) at the shelf centre, and when the fingers stayed locked in the ring wall tried several release motions. Finally I set it back down resting on the shelf and finished.

steps.what: Read the robot description and the scene (step 0)
steps.why: Know the arm, gripper and cameras before planning
steps.result: agilex_piper_sim: 6 joints; parallel-jaw gripper (stroke 0.07 m, max width 0.066 m, closing axis y, approach axis z, tip reach 0.02 m, closed_empty 0.97, held_below 0.93); cameras left/right (scene) and wrist; 2250 steps at 15 Hz. Two objects: obj1 green ring, obj2 black box.

steps.what: Measured the ring and the shelf from object points: circle fit, radial percentiles, heightmaps
steps.why: The tape is wider than the gripper, so I needed the wall geometry for a rim grasp and the shelf's top surface for placing
steps.result: Ring centre (0.2534, -0.0069), inner radius 0.033, outer 0.045, top z 0.025. Shelf top flat at z 0.080.

steps.what: Checked IK and collisions for rim grasps at -y, +y, -x and +x; inspected the finger collision spheres
steps.why: Pick a reachable grasp whose arm links clear the scene
steps.result: All reachable. +x put link6 into the shelf. The finger spheres cover each finger's whole stroke, so finger contacts with the ring were expected. Chose -y with yaw 90.

steps.what: Moved to pre-grasp at z 0.10 (step 42), projected the planned finger spots onto the wrist image, descended to z 0.027 (step 73)
steps.result: The projected ring matched the real ring in the wrist camera. The arm landed about 5 mm short in x (tracking error, tangent to the wall). Left and right views showed the fingers straddling the wall.

Reading 0.808 (13.5 mm gap): held. The wrist images (010 vs 013) show the ring moved as the fingers closed. I did not act on this then. Later fits showed it had rotated about 35 deg about the grip, so the closing axis was far from radial.

steps.what: Previewed a straight lift to z 0.17, then swept IK reachability for top-down poses
steps.result: Refused as unreachable. Top-down reaches only z <= 0.13 at x 0.25 and z <= 0.08 at the shelf centre, so I planned a pitched place.

Ring held level (about 2 deg tilt). Perception dropped it ('floating segments hugging the robot dropped'), so I located it from green scene-camera points: centre at TCP + (0.022, 0.032), i.e. rotated in the grip.

steps.what: Carried to pre-place over the shelf at 20 deg pitch (step 159), measured the ring, compensated tracking error, descended to place at 15 deg pitch (step 193)
steps.why: Put the ring centre at the shelf centre (0.4295, -0.0184) with its low edge about 5 mm above the top
steps.result: The ring model from the actual TCP matched the measured ring within 2 mm. At the place pose the ring centre was (0.4297, -0.0162), its bottom 4-6 mm above the shelf.

steps.why: Drop the ring onto the shelf
steps.result: Failure. The gripper opened fully (reading 0.0) but the ring stayed suspended about 1 cm above the shelf, tilted 11 deg, shifted +8 mm in y. It was hanging on the inner finger, which on opening had swept along a short chord near the narrow end of the hole because the grip was oblique.

steps.what: Nudged the gripper +1.2 cm x / -0.6 cm y (step 230)
steps.why: Move the inner finger toward the hole centre to free it
steps.result: The ring moved with the gripper (+1.7 cm), bringing its +x edge to within about 4 mm of the shelf's far edge. Not freed.

steps.what: Re-closed (step 245), modelled the ring from its measured pose, carried it to the shelf centre at 5 deg pitch so it hung flat, lowered 5 mm and opened (steps 291-325)
steps.why: Get back to a known state, then release with the ring flat and nearly touching the shelf
steps.result: The ring hung flat (0.1 deg) just above the shelf. On opening, the gripper stopped at 0.722 (19.5 mm), blocked by the ring. The ring rested on the shelf but stayed attached.

steps.what: Diagnostics and release attempts (steps 340-509): close (0.87, 9.1 mm); annulus fit; open + rise 4 mm; gripper(0.8); open + back off 1.2 cm in -x; quick 3.5 cm lift in 0.45 s; close in the air
steps.why: Find a motion that frees the fingers
steps.result: The annulus fit put the TCP inside the ring's -x wall (4.15 cm from the ring centre) with the closing axis tangent to the wall, and both fingers apparently embedded in the wall's collision shape. gripper(0.8) was treated as a full close (the command is binary). The ring followed every motion, including the quick lift and the close in the air.

steps.what: Set the ring back down on the shelf, commanded the gripper open, took the final look from left, right and wrist, re-perceived, finished (step 558)
steps.why: Leave the best achievable final state: tape resting on the shelf
steps.result: Ring flat (1.4 deg) on the shelf top, footprint x 0.374-0.464, y -0.076-0.014, inside the shelf top. The gripper is still in contact at the ring's -x wall (reading 0.72). Used 558 of 2250 steps, about 32 min of wall time.

diagnosis: The tape ends on the shelf (flat, fully inside the top face), but the gripper never let go: its fingers remain locked in the ring's -x wall. A judge that requires a release would score this as a failure. Chain of causes: (1) When the gripper closed on the wall at step 88, the closing force (with the TCP about 5 mm off the planned point because of arm tracking error) rotated the ring about 35 deg about the grip. The gap reading (13.5 mm, against about 12 mm expected for a radial grip) and the wrist images (010 vs 013) showed this, but I did not stop to re-grasp. (2) Because of that oblique grip, opening at the place pose drove the inner finger along a short chord near the narrow end of the ring's hole instead of toward its centre. The ring hung on the finger instead of dropping (images 024, 030). Opening while the ring was still about 5 mm up and pitched, rather than already resting on the shelf, made this worse. (3) Re-closing at that location left both fingers interlocked with the ring's -x wall, apparently embedded in its collision shape: the closing axis was tangent to the wall and the TCP sat inside it. From then on the ring followed every arm motion and both gripper states, and the gripper command is binary, so no partial opening was possible. What I would do differently: after closing, fit the ring's pose relative to the TCP (wrist plus scene cameras) and re-grasp on the table if the closing axis is not radial. Lower the ring until it actually rests on the shelf before opening. Never open with a finger inside the hole unless the opening direction points at the hole's centre with clearance.
lessons: For a ring or roll gripped at its rim, the release sends the inner finger across the hole. It is safe only if the closing axis is radial, so the finger moves toward the hole centre. Verify that alignment right after the close and again before opening.

Read the gripper gap against the expected wall thickness: a larger gap (13.5 vs 12 mm) meant an oblique grip. Wrist images before and after the close showed the object moving in the grip. Re-grasp before lifting rather than continuing.

On this PiPER, top-down poses reach only z <= 0.08 at x about 0.42 and z <= 0.13 at x about 0.25. Placing on a raised surface needs a pitched gripper. Pitching about the closing axis keeps a radially gripped ring's centre fixed.

Arm tracking error is 3-10 mm and changes sign with the direction of motion. Measure the actual TCP after each move and compensate the next target. A ring model built from the measured pose predicted the real ring within 2 mm.
Perception drops a held object ('floating segment hugging the robot'). Locate it from colour-filtered scene-camera points (circle or annulus fit, plane fit for tilt), not from objects().
The gripper command is binary: gripper(0.8) acts as closed.
Release with the object already resting on the support (lower until contact) rather than dropping it from a few mm while pitched.

Once fingers are interlocked with an object in sim, gripper open/close cycles, small and quick lifts, and lateral moves all drag the object along. Avoid getting into that state: it is very hard to undo.
